_note: uv sync --extra crafter (crafter-gym, gym/crafter/, pulls crafter), then pip install --force-reinstall 'crafter @ git+https://github.com/chengfanbrain/crafter.git@deterministic' -- a fork of 1.8.3 whose single change is that a seed plus an action list replays exactly. Plain PyPI crafter runs this config fine and plays identically to a subject, but its blocks cannot be replayed, so a model cannot be given the same episode. This is the paradigm's level 1 (affordance): nothing hostile exists, the four life stats are frozen at 9 and hidden from the HUD, and nothing but lava can kill. What is left is what the world affords -- which materials give way to a bare hand, what a table makes reachable -- learnt without a clock running out. The rules are the env's (gym/crafter/crafter_gym/levels.py, 'level' in env_kwargs below) and not this file's, so a model meets the same game: see _level_note.
_shared_notes: Every field of the game phase below is level 4's, except env_kwargs.level, resume, rewind, tasks, and the page above the game. The last two are on this phase and on no other: rewind because this is the one level whose deaths are rolled back, tasks because this is the one level that asks for the holds in seconds rather than taking the rig's defaults, and each has its own note below. The notes that explain those shared fields -- the eight buttons and the menu, turn-based pacing, frame size, savestate stride, the live HUD, the score line, the three cues, and why there is one interface for all of them -- are in configs/dbp_games/crafter__crafter_L4.json and are deliberately not copied here, because four copies of a paragraph drift apart and the one thing a level is allowed to change is the game.
_level_note: The level is a gymnasium.Wrapper under the menu (crafter_gym.levels.LevelWrapper), and the table it reads is the rig's own (crafter-for-brain-scan v0.33, core.py:LEVELS), field for field. L1 is hostiles=False, homeostatic_death=False, hidden_items=(health, food, drink, energy), frozen_stats=True. In practice: zombies, skeletons and arrows are cleared out of the world worldgen just made and the engine's ten-step creature rebalance is filtered so none come back; _update_life_stats is a no-op, so hunger, thirst and fatigue never move food, drink or energy off 9; a health decrement from a missing necessity is refused; the four icons are blanked out of the item panel without moving any other icon, since the engine skips an item below 1 and draws the rest at their own index; and the sleep button, which stock crafter ignores at full energy, is honoured as a one-tick nap so it is not a silent no-op in the one level whose energy never drops. Two things still end an episode: lava, which zeroes health in the action phase before any of these rules run, and nothing else. Death itself is unchanged in every level: health cannot regenerate from 0 (stock crafter can add a point on the very tick a death set it there, which would make the episode's end unreliable), and the view is tinted red while the player is dead, which is the engine's own commented-out tint and the one death signal that survives a hidden health icon. The same seed gives the same terrain in all four levels: a peaceful world is a world generated like any other with the hostiles deleted afterwards, so worldgen draws the same randomness either way.
_tasks_note: tasks is how long the two completion messages are held, and the chain they are about is the level's (gym/crafter/crafter_gym/tasks.py:TASK_CHAIN, the rig's own order and wording from core.py). One entry at a time is named in the middle of the HUD strip, and the fraction at its right counts the entries reached out of what this level can reach. Reaching one freezes the frame twice: 'Task completed! Score +1' for tasks.done, then 'Next task: ...' for tasks.next, which are the rig's --task-done-s and --task-hold-s defaults. Both are paid out of the block's own clock rather than added to it, so a block that holds ends a few presses earlier and the scan's timing is untouched; set either to 0 to say nothing. The chain is a wrapper around the env and not a feature of the adapter for the usual reason: a rollout of this level is given the same task, in the same order, out of the same ``info``, so the model and the subject are asked for the same thing (AGENTS.md rule 1). Eleven of the twelve entries are achievements crafter scores itself; build a stone shelter is the one it has no achievement for, so the chain tests it (a sealed room the player can stand in, small enough that nothing can spawn beside them and shut against an arrow) and counts it at both ends of the fraction, which is why this level shows 21 and not 20. The menu's last entry puts the current task off to the back of this episode's order, for a subject stuck on one: it costs a turn per press like any other menu gesture and gives the engine no action.
_not_here_note: What the rig's level-1 session has and this block does not: the stat tasks (core.py:STAT_TASKS), which cut into the chain with drink water, eat a cow or sleep whenever a life stat runs low. They need a stat that moves and this level freezes all four at 9, so they belong to L2 along with the homeostat they read; LEVELS carries the 'stat_tasks' flag and nothing reads it.
_rewind_note: rewind is the rig's rollback-on-death for L1 (core.py:DEATH_RESTORE_LEVELS, --death-restore-s default 1.0 s at cadence_hz 5.0, --death-hold-s default 1.2), and it is a phase field beside resume rather than a LEVELS entry for the rig's own reason: the table defines the rules an agent's training env must share, while rolling a death back is session policy, so a rollout of this level keeps the standard reset-on-death episode and the two players still meet the same game. Fan's rationale in the rig: re-collecting wood after a lava slip is boring, and the scan wants exploration and learning rather than repeated early-chain grinding. The window is frames and not seconds because this block is turn-based: the world moves only when the subject presses, so a second of the run clock is worth one press or none, while a frame is one of the subject's own moves whatever they spent deciding. One move and not five: --death-restore-s 1.0 at cadence_hz 5.0 is five of the rig's ticks, but the rig pushes a snapshot on every tick and a tick steps the env whether or not a button is down (core.py:Rig.tick, and ButtonMapper.resolve answers noop for no buttons), so what its second goes back is whichever presses happened to fall inside it rather than five of them. Tested on L1 and settled on 2026-10-02. The death frame holds 1.2 s first with 'You died' written over it, so the red tint and the word are both seen before the world moves: a rolled-back death never reaches the outcome screen, which is where that line is otherwise said. Only the three other levels keep the true death: L2-L4 have no rewind field. What it costs the record: each rollback writes the world it went back to on its own line, so an episode is replayed as segments cut at those lines rather than as one action list (fmri_gym/replay.py), and the frames between the rollback and where it went back to are in the log as played and then undone.
_cue_open_question: cues is true, as in level 4, so a press the engine refused makes a sound. In a level whose whole point is learning what works that is arguably a hint rather than feedback. It is left on because an L1 that differs from L4 in more than its rules is harder to compare, and because the subject can hear it in the rig too; turn it off here if the pilot says the sound is doing the learning.
_resume_note: resume names the thread of play this block continues, and the block picks up the world the last block of the same name left off in, but only when the block's clock was what stopped the episode: a death or a forfeit ends that world and the next block opens a new one from its seed. On this level a death is rolled back rather than an ending (see _rewind_note) and no max_rewinds caps that, so a lava slip never ends the thread of play here: what reaches the slot is a world the subject may have died in several times and come back from, and what still ends it is a restart or a forfeit from the menu. The name is this level's own, because all four levels are the same env id (CrafterMenu-v0) and one shared name would hand L4's world to an L1 block. 300 s of turn-based play is a first morning, and the tech tree a level-1 subject is here to learn is longer than that, so without this a session is five first mornings. The level is carried in env_kwargs, so it is in the slot file's header too: a block whose level does not match the world it is about to continue is told so by name before it plays (fmri_gym/resume.py:env_drift). What comes back is the world's own rules and not this config's, because restore replaces the env the block just built -- which is the whole reason a level is a wrapper's parameter and not a patch an adapter applies to a live player.
_instructions_note: The page is level 4's with its opening lines replaced by the rig's own (core.py:INSTRUCTIONS page 1: explore and try things, the game shows you what works), which is what L1 is. The controls are the same eight buttons and the same menu, so a subject who practised in the rig keeps their fingers. No page mentions the life stats, hidden or otherwise, and none names a mechanic: what a rule does is the game's job to show. In a session that plays the levels in order these lines are where the rig's LEVEL_INTROS go, except that the rig shows them between levels ('The next rounds are different') while a config played on its own has to say it up front.

text: Crafter
Explore the world and try things.
The game itself will show you what works.
The world waits for you: it moves one step each
time you press a button, and not otherwise.
One task at a time is named above the game. Reach
it and the game says so, and names the next one.
Controls (8 buttons):
ARROWS      move
D           interact / attack / collect
S           sleep
W           next menu item
A           do the menu item
The menu holds the ten actions with no button of
their own: place stone, table, furnace, plant, and
make a wood / stone / iron pickaxe or sword. Last
in it is skip task, which puts your current task
off until later. W moves the cursor and shows it
over your character; A performs it. Moving the
cursor also costs a turn.
(press SPACE to start)
